questions.prompt: Which of the following is considered a user interface component?

options.text: The border of a text input field.

questions.explanation: Borders, icons, and buttons are graphical components that require a clear boundary so interactions can be identified.
questions.hint: Think about the parts of a form that are actually clicked.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Identify what qualifies as a user interface component.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum contrast ratio required for non-text components like icons and borders?
questions.explanation: Graphical objects and user interface states require a threshold of 3 against their adjacent colors.
questions.hint: It is the lower of the two standard thresholds.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Understand the 3 ratio requirement for borders and icons.

questions.prompt: How can adjacent slices in a pie chart be made distinguishable?

options.text: By ensuring the slices maintain a contrast ratio of at least 3, or by adding dark borders between them.
By making all the slices the exact same color.
By removing all labels and legends from the chart.
By ensuring the slices have a contrast ratio of 1 to 1.

questions.explanation: If adjacent colors do not meet the ratio of 3, they blend together. A dark border provides the necessary boundary.
questions.hint: Consider how to physically separate two similar colors touching each other.
questions.testedLearningPoint: Apply contrast rules to data visualizations and charts.
